examples.question_text: Rewrite $\sin 128^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
Rewrite $\cos 112^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}A&=180^{\circ}-112^{\circ}\\&=68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

In Q2, the $x$-coordinate is negative, so cosine is negative.

$\begin{aligned}\cos 112^{\circ}&=-\cos 68^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

examples.question_text: Rewrite $\tan 146^{\circ}$ in terms of its acute reference angle.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}A&=180^{\circ}-146^{\circ}\\&=34^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

In Q2, sine is positive and cosine is negative. Their ratio, tangent, is negative.

$\begin{aligned}\tan 146^{\circ}&=-\tan 34^{\circ}\end{aligned}$

coverage.summary: Authored six examples covering reference-angle rewriting and exact-value evaluation for sine, cosine and tangent in Q2. Every adaptation changes the angle from its mapped source item. Separate editable prompts and solutions use single-dollar aligned mathematics; prose inherits the renderer's blue. The solution-only unit-circle diagram illustrates supplementary angles without exposing answers in a prompt. Independent equations have no phantom equals. All 30 retained assessments are mapped by method only; their mathematics was neither changed nor re-audited. Independent example review and actual rendering verification remain for the coordinator.

examples.derivation: 180°−128°=52°. In Q2, y>0, so sin128°=sin52°. The diagram places P at 128°, with the reference arc spanning 180° to 128° and a perpendicular to the x-axis.
180°−112°=68°. In Q2, x<0, so cos112°=−cos68°. This follows the source's supplement-and-sign method.
180°−146°=34°. In Q2, sinθ>0 and cosθ<0, so their quotient is negative: tan146°=−tan34°.
180°−135°=45°. Sine is positive in Q2; sin135°=sin45°=1/√2.
180°−120°=60°. Cosine is negative in Q2; cos120°=−cos60°=−1/2.
180°−150°=30°. Tangent is negative in Q2; tan150°=−tan30°=−1/√3.

review.summary: All six examples pass independent mathematical, source and scope review. The 30 exact assessment locators correctly map to six covered methods without repeating the accepted assessment audit. Every adaptation changes its mapped source angle. The solution-only planar diagram uses the standard palette and explicit 10 pt labels; final rendered sizing remains for the capture stage. No syllabus exception is needed.
